text: Each row in the main table MUST show `http://localhost:P`, where `P` is that forward's actual local port. Clicking the URL MUST open that forward in the system's default browser.
Pressing `b` MUST open `http://localhost:P` in the system's default browser, where `P` is the actual local port of the selected port forward.
The `piraeus` executable MUST use `clap` to parse its command-line arguments before starting the terminal UI.
Pressing `i` on a row with an error MUST show more diagnostic detail within the TUI without opening a modal dialog.

When an action on a port forward fails, or its SSH process stops unexpectedly, the affected table row MUST show a brief error and be highlighted in red. Failures MUST NOT interrupt the user with a modal dialog.

Pressing `a` MUST begin an add-forward flow with separate host, remote-port, and local-port stages, in that order. Completing the local-port stage with valid selections MUST start the forward and add it to the table.

The host stage MUST list hosts discovered from the user's SSH configuration and an `Other` entry, with one option visibly selected. `↑` and `↓` MUST move the selection. Typing host-name characters MUST select `Other` and enter a custom host name; the user MUST also be able to select `Other` with the arrow keys. Pressing `Enter` with a discovered host or a nonempty custom host MUST advance to the remote-port stage.

The local-port stage MUST show the applicable radio-style local-port choices with one visibly selected. `↑` and `↓` MUST move the selection. Typing digits MUST select the manual local-port choice and enter an alternative local port without a focus change. Pressing `Enter` with a valid choice MUST complete the add-forward flow.

The application MUST remember the most recently confirmed remote ports across application runs. It MUST store this history at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/piraeus/config.toml` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is an absolute path; when it is unset, empty, or relative, it MUST use the XDG default `~/.config/piraeus/config.toml`. If that file is absent, it MUST import recent ports from an existing `~/.piraeus.toml`, `~/.pfm.toml`, or `pfm/config.toml` in the selected XDG configuration directory and save them to the new path before presenting recent choices.

The remote-port stage MUST list distinct remote ports confirmed earlier in this or a previous application run, most recent first, including ports whose forwards were removed. It MUST include an `Other` entry and remain usable when there are no recent ports. `↑` and `↓` MUST move the selection. Typing digits MUST select `Other` and enter a custom remote port without a focus change. Pressing `Enter` with a valid selected port MUST advance to the local-port stage.
When the entered remote port is free on localhost, the add-forward dialog MUST initially select that same port as the local port and MUST also offer a user-specified alternative.

Before presenting local-port choices, the application MUST determine whether the preferred local port is free, occupied by an application-managed forward, or occupied by another process. On a conflict, it MUST suggest the first free local port found by incrementing the preferred port repeatedly (for example, checking `8031`, then `8032` after a conflict on `8030`).

The host picker MUST use `ssh2-config` to read `Host` declarations in the user's `~/.ssh/config` and find selectable host names. It MUST use the parsed configuration only to collect literal names; wildcard patterns and negated patterns MUST NOT appear as selectable hosts. For example, `Host chronos mnemosyne` contributes two names, while `Host *` contributes none.

If an application-managed forward occupies the preferred local port, the dialog MUST offer three mutually exclusive choices: replace that forward on the preferred port, use the suggested free port, or enter an alternative local port. It MUST initially select the suggested free port. If the user chooses replacement, the application MUST stop the existing managed SSH process before starting the new forward and MUST update the table so the replaced forward is no longer shown as running.
( ) Use local port 8030, replacing existing forward

If a manually entered local port is already occupied, the add-forward dialog MUST show that conflict and require the user to choose a free port before confirming. It MUST NOT stop the occupying process.

In every add-forward case, the dialog MUST offer a radio choice that lets the user enter an alternative **local** port explicitly. The entered remote port MUST remain unchanged when the user chooses an alternative local port.

The add-forward dialog MUST accept only whole-number remote and manually entered local ports from 1 through 65535. It MUST explain invalid input inside the dialog and MUST NOT start or replace a forward while the input is invalid.
Pressing `q` while the main table has focus MUST stop all port forwards managed by the application and then exit the TUI.
Pressing `r` MUST stop the SSH processes for all listed port forwards that are running and attempt to recreate every listed port forward, including those currently in an error state.
Pressing `x` MUST stop the selected managed port forward, if it is running, and remove its row from the table.

The application MUST create local port forwards through SSH, connecting a port on localhost to the same service port on the selected remote SSH host. It MUST track the SSH processes it starts so that subsequent actions affect only port forwards it manages.
For example, a forward for `chronos` remote port `3000` using local port `3001` makes the remote service available at `localhost:3001`.

The application MUST delegate interpretation of SSH configuration settings to OpenSSH commands: `ssh` when connecting and `ssh -G <host>` when it needs the effective configuration for a supplied host name. Apart from discovering names in `Host` declarations, it MUST NOT use the parsed configuration to determine connection settings.

The table MUST show a new or refreshed forward as running only after its SSH process has established the chosen local listener. If startup fails, the row MUST show an error for the attempted host and ports.
The suggested-port search MUST stop at port 65535. If it finds no free higher port, the add-forward dialog MUST explain that no suggested port is available and MUST still allow manual port entry.

If a process outside the application occupies the preferred local port, the dialog MUST offer the suggested free port and a user-specified alternative. It MUST initially select the suggested free port, MUST NOT offer to replace the other process, and MUST NOT stop it.
Pressing `?` MUST show the available keystrokes and their actions, including how to select a row and the `a`, `b`, `x`, `q`, `r`, and `i` commands.
The `piraeus` Cargo package MUST provide a binary target named `piraeus` and MUST NOT provide a library target.
The application MUST let the user select a table row with the keyboard. Actions that refer to a selected port forward MUST use the visibly selected row.

The main view MUST be a table of port forwards managed by the application. Each row MUST show the SSH host, remote port, actual local port, and current state. A failed forwarding attempt MUST remain in the table so its error is visible.
| SSH host | Remote port | Local port | State |
The application MUST run as an interactive text user interface in a terminal.

The exact requirements inputs snapshot `requirements.browser.link`, `requirements.browser.open`, `requirements.cli.argument_parsing`, `requirements.errors.info`, `requirements.errors.visible`, `requirements.forwarding.add`, `requirements.forwarding.add.host`, `requirements.forwarding.add.local_port`, `requirements.forwarding.add.port_history`, `requirements.forwarding.add.remote_port`, `requirements.forwarding.default_local_port`, `requirements.forwarding.detect_conflict`, `requirements.forwarding.host_discovery`, `requirements.forwarding.managed_conflict_choices`, `requirements.forwarding.manual_conflict`, `requirements.forwarding.manual_local_port`, `requirements.forwarding.port_validation`, `requirements.forwarding.quit`, `requirements.forwarding.refresh`, `requirements.forwarding.remove`, `requirements.forwarding.ssh`, `requirements.forwarding.ssh_config`, `requirements.forwarding.startup_state`, `requirements.forwarding.suggestion_exhausted`, `requirements.forwarding.unmanaged_conflict_choices`, `requirements.help.shortcuts`, `requirements.packaging.binary_only`, `requirements.tui.selection`, `requirements.tui.table`, `requirements.tui.terminal`, which are the applicable cited definitions. The cited texts jointly account for this function's behavior; no additional definition governs a separate effect of this function.
